what: CRH supplies building materials: cement, aggregates, asphalt and ready-mixed concrete, and it also builds roads and infrastructure itself. North America is its largest market and it moved its primary listing to New York.
customers: Road agencies and departments of transportation, infrastructure contractors, housebuilders and commercial developers.
money: aggregates, cement, asphalt and paving services in North America
precast, building envelope and outdoor living products
materials and products in Europe and Australia
moat: Quarries and cement plants close to the roads they serve: aggregates are too heavy to transport far, so each site has a local monopoly on cost.
risks: Infrastructure spending depends on government budgets
Residential construction is weak while mortgage rates are high
Debt of about $21 billion funds continuous acquisitions
Energy costs are a large input for cement
opportunities: US federal infrastructure funding supports multi-year road and bridge demand
Bundling materials with paving services captures more of each project
Pricing has risen faster than costs for several years
watch: Pricing in Americas Materials and the backlog of infrastructure work.
